UNAUDITED: W18 probe output; not a proved project claim. Pinned HEAD in PINNED_HEAD.txt.
change: Proof emission switched from pysat's in-memory Lingeling get_proof() to cadical run AS A BINARY writing its own DRAT file, and replay now runs two independent checkers.

binaries.solver: computations/unaudited-hygiene-h1-2026-08-15/tools/cadical/build/cadical (CaDiCaL 3.0.1, built from source by the H1 hygiene lane)
binaries.checker_secondary: rup18 (this lane's own forward RUP/DRUP checker)
binaries.note: w18_sweep.HAVE_NATIVE gates the path; if the binaries are ever missing the code falls back to the pysat path and stamps the row emitter='pysat-lingeling-get_proof (NATIVE BINARY MISSING)' so the fallback can never hide.

invocation: cadical --binary=false -q <cnf> <proof.drup>   (rc 20 = UNSAT, rc 10 = SAT, anything else = PROOF-EMIT-ERROR); then drat-trim <cnf> <proof> -I -t 20000 must print 's VERIFIED', and rup18 must exit 0 for proofs under 1500 MB.
acceptance: a row is 'verified' only when the proof terminates in the empty clause AND drat-trim says VERIFIED AND rup18 exits 0 (rup18 skipped only above 1500 MB, where drat-trim is the checker).

backfill.tool: run_reemit.py -- re-solves the STORED CNF (certificates/m{m}/m{m}_g{mask}.cnf.gz) with cadical and replaces only the .drup.gz, and only when the new proof verifies; the .cnf.gz is never touched and its SHA-256 is re-checked first.
backfill.why_the_stored_CNF_is_the_right_input: the formula is what the verified kill certificates justify; a fresh CEGAR run would build a different (equally valid) formula and would race the sweep for the same artefact filenames.
backfill.plan: re-emit the two failed proofs first, then the >=40 MB tail (the ones the cold ledger cannot afford to replay), then the remainder -- the distribution is skewed enough that re-emitting all 662 natively is affordable, so the 0.45% defect rate does not have to be trusted.

defect_rate_that_motivated_this: 3 corrupt proofs in ~660 pysat emissions (m18 7847550, m18 15433212, m19 15449727); all three were caught by replay, none affected a mathematical verdict.
